papers.title: Bayesian kernel-based system identification with quantized output data
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a novel method for linear system identification with quantized output data. We model the impulse response as a zero-mean Gaussian process whose covariance (kernel) is given by the recently proposed stable spline kernel, which encodes information on regularity and exponential stability. This serves as a starting point to cast our system identification problem into a Bayesian framework. We employ Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to provide an estimate of the system. In particular, we show how to design a Gibbs sampler which quickly converges to the target distribution. Numerical simulations show a substantial improvement in the accuracy of the estimates over state-of-the-art kernel-based methods when employed in identification of systems with quantized data.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文将贝叶斯核方法与MCMC用于量化输出系统辨识，其不确定性量化思路对FEA替代建模有潜在借鉴价值，但未涉及结构优化或生物力学应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modelling, does not handle design constraints, and is not applied to biomechanics or implant problems.

summary_zh.method: 利用稳定样条核作为高斯过程先验，结合MCMC进行贝叶斯推断
summary_zh.result: 估计精度显著优于现有核方法
summary_zh.validation: 通过数值仿真对比基准方法

summary_en.motivation: To improve the accuracy of linear system identification when output data are quantized.
summary_en.method: A Bayesian framework is adopted with a zero-mean Gaussian process prior using the stable spline kernel, and a Gibbs sampler is designed for efficient MCMC inference.
summary_en.result: The proposed method achieves substantial accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art kernel-based methods in numerical experiments.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulations on benchmark examples demonstrate the performance gain.

papers.title: Autonomy and Reliability of Continuous Active Learning for Technology-Assisted Review
papers.abstract: We enhance the autonomy of the continuous active learning method shown by Cormack and Grossman (SIGIR 2014) to be effective for technology-assisted review, in which documents from a collection are retrieved and reviewed, using relevance feedback, until substantially all of the relevant documents have been reviewed. Autonomy is enhanced through the elimination of topic-specific and dataset-specific tuning parameters, so that the sole input required by the user is, at the outset, a short query, topic description, or single relevant document; and, throughout the review, ongoing relevance assessments of the retrieved documents. We show that our enhancements consistently yield superior results to Cormack and Grossman's version of continuous active learning, and other methods, not only on average, but on the vast majority of topics from four separate sets of tasks: the legal datasets examined by Cormack and Grossman, the Reuters RCV1-v2 subject categories, the TREC 6 AdHoc task, and the construction of the TREC 2002 filtering test collection.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于文本检索的主动学习，与有限元代理建模或植入物设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses text document retrieval and active learning, with no connection to finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, or biomechanical design.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高技术辅助审查中连续主动学习方法的自主性
summary_zh.method: 消除主题和数据集特定的调参，只依赖用户初始查询和相关性评估
summary_zh.result: 在多个数据集上表现优于原始方法
summary_zh.validation: 在四个不同任务集上进行了实证比较

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the autonomy of continuous active learning for technology-assisted document review by removing dataset-specific tuning.
summary_en.method: Eliminates all topic-specific and dataset-specific parameters, requiring only an initial query and ongoing relevance feedback.
summary_en.result: The enhanced method consistently outperforms the original version across four diverse document collections.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on legal datasets, Reuters RCV1-v2, TREC 6 AdHoc, and TREC 2002 filtering tasks.
